## Packages {.sparse-slide}

Load the standard packages.

```{r}
#| message: false
#| label: load

library(tidyverse) 
library(haven) # not core tidyverse
library(gssr)
library(gssrdoc) # load the GSS codebook
library(summarytools)
```

## Load your data

```{r}
#| message: false
#| label: gssdata

# Get the data all survey years
data(gss_all)

```

# dplyr II {.theme-section}

## `select()` {.sparse-slide}

Use `select()` to choose columns in a dataframe.\

<br>

. . .

```{r}
#| label: select
#| code-line-numbers: "1|2|5"
#| output-location: fragment

my_data <- gss_all |>  # <1>
  select(year, agekdbrn, childs, hrs1) # <2>

# look at the first rows & columns of the dataframe
head(my_data) # <3>

```

1.  Save a new data frame
2.  Keep only the listed variables

::: notes
:::

## `head()` & `tail()` {.smaller .sparse-slide}

`head()` looks at the first few column names and **first** few rows of your df.  
`tail()` looks at the first few column names and **last** few rows of your df.

<br>

. . .

```{r}
#| label: head

# look at the first rows & columns of the data frame
head(my_data)

```

## Mini-task {.sparse-slide}

::: task
{{< fa check-double >}} Use `tail()` to look at the last few rows of `my_data`
:::

<br>

. . .

```{r}
#| label: tail

# look at the first rows & LAST columns of the data frame
tail(my_data)

```


## Mini-task {.sparse-slide}

::: task
{{< fa check-double >}} Create a dataframe with the variables `year`,
`agekdbrn`, `childs`, and `hrs1`, including only respondents
from the year 2022 who have no missing values in any of these variables.
:::

<br>

. . .

```{r}
#| label: select-mini-task
#| code-line-numbers: "1-2|3|4|6"
#| output-location: slide

my_data <- gss_all |> 
  select(year, agekdbrn, childs, hrs1) |>
  filter(year == 2022) |>
  drop_na() # <1>

head(my_data) 

```

1.  No need to list all variables inside drop_na()

::: notes
[ASK:]{style="color: #6f42c1"}\
:::

## `mutate()` {.sparse-slide}

Use `mutate()` to add new columns or change existing ones.

<br>

. . .

```{r}
#| label: mutate
#| code-line-numbers: "1-2|3"
#| output-location: fragment

# Use mutate to create a new variable: annual_hrs1
my_data <- my_data |>
  mutate(annual_hrs1 = hrs1 * 52)

head(my_data)
```

## Mini-task {.sparse-slide}

::: task
{{< fa lightbulb >}} Use `mutate()`, `mean()`, and `sd()` to create a
column with Z scores for `hrs1`
:::

<br>

. . .

```{r}
#| label: mutate-mini-task
#| code-line-numbers: "1|3-5"
#| output-location: slide

my_data <- my_data|>
  # Create Z-score for annual_hours
  mutate(z_hrs1 = (hrs1 - mean(hrs1)) / 
           sd(hrs1) 
  )

head(my_data)

```

## `mutate()` & logical variables {.sparse-slide}

```{r}
#| label: mutate-logical
#| code-line-numbers: "1-2"
#| output-location: fragment

my_data <- my_data|>
  mutate(teen_parent = (agekdbrn < 18) * 1) # <1>
  
head(my_data)
  
```

1.  Returns a logical vector (TRUE, FALSE, or NA) and \* 1 converts it
    to numeric

::: aside
`agekdbrn`: How old were you when your first child was born?
:::

## Code Meets Question {.sparse-slide background-image="images/gears-solid-full.png" background-size="80px" background-repeat="repeat"}

::: task
{{< fa lightbulb >}} What proportion of new parents were teenagers
(e.g., under 18 years old)?
:::

<br>

. . .

```{r}
#| label: mutate-logical-CMQ
#| code-line-numbers: "1|2"
#| output-location: fragment

my_data |> 
  summarise(proportion = mean(teen_parent)) # <1>
  
```

1.  Mean of the variable, which equals the proportion of `1s`

::: aside
`agekdbrn`: How old were you when your first child was born?
:::

## Mini-task {.sparse-slide}

::: task
{{< fa lightbulb >}} Use `mutate()` and `summarise()` to determine what
proportion of new parents were older than 40 years old.
:::

<br>

. . .

```{r}
my_data |>

```

## `mutate()` with `case_when()` {.sparse-slide}

Use `case_when()` inside `mutate()` to create values based on
conditions.

<br>

. . .

```{r}
#| label: mutate-case-when
#| code-line-numbers: "1|2-3|4|5|6|7-8|10-11"
#| output-location: slide

my_data <-  my_data |>  
# Use mutate to create a new variable: childs_3cat
  mutate(childs_3cat = case_when(
    childs == 1 ~ "1 kid",
    childs == 2 ~ "2 kids",
    childs >  3 ~ "3+ kids",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_)
  ) 

# Always double check your work!
table(my_data$childs, my_data$childs_3cat)
```

## Code Meets Question {.sparse-slide background-image="images/gears-solid-full.png" background-size="80px" background-repeat="repeat"}

::: task
{{< fa lightbulb >}} What proportion of new parents had their first
child in their teens, 20s, 30s, or after age 40?
:::

<br>

. . .

```{r}
#| label: mutate01
#| code-line-numbers: "1|2|3|4|5|6|7-8|10-11"
#| output-location: slide

my_data <-  my_data |>  
  mutate(age_groups = case_when(
    agekdbrn < 18 ~ "<18",
    agekdbrn >= 18 & agekdbrn <= 29 ~ "18–29",
    agekdbrn >= 30 & agekdbrn <= 39 ~ "30–39",
    agekdbrn >= 40 ~ "40+",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_)
  ) 

my_data |>
  freq(age_groups, report.nas = FALSE, headings = FALSE)
```

::: notes
[ASK: Tell me what this output means in a
sentence.]{style="color: #6f42c1"}\
:::

# Overwriting data {.theme-section}

## Overwriting & assignment operators

::: {.callout-tip icon="false"}
## {{< fa hat-wizard >}} Heads Up!

Overwriting datasets and variables can be intentional or unintentional.
:::

<br>

Let's make a tiny data frame to use as an example:

```{r}
#| label: tibble
#| output-location: column-fragment

df <- tibble(
        x = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5), 
        y = c("a", "a", "b", "c", "c")
      )

df
```

## {.sparse-slide data-menu-title="Assignment operators"}

Suppose you run the following and **then** you inspect `df`.

::: {style="font-family: 'Shadows Into Light'"}
Will the `x` variable have values [1, 2, 3, 4,
5]{style="color: #18bc9c"} or [2, 4, 6, 8, 10]{style="color: #F39C12"}?
:::

<br>

::::: columns
::: column
```{r}
#| label: no-assignment

df |>
  mutate(x = x * 2)
```
:::

::: {.column .fragment}
```{r}
#| label: no-assignment-results
df
```
:::
:::::

. . .

> **Do something and show me**


## {.sparse-slide data-menu-title="Assignment operators (cont)"}

Suppose you run the following and **then** you inspect `df`.

::: {style="font-family: 'Shadows Into Light'"}
Will the `x` variable have values [1, 2, 3, 4,
5]{style="color: #18bc9c"} or [2, 4, 6, 8, 10]{style="color: #F39C12"}?
:::

<br>

::::: columns
::: {.column .fragment}
```{r}
#| label: assignment

df <- df |>
  mutate(x = x * 2)
```
:::

::: {.column .fragment}
```{r}
#| label: assignment-results
#| code-line-numbers: "1"

df
```
:::
:::::

. . .

> **Do something, save result, overwriting original**

## {.smaller .sparse-slide data-menu-title="Assignment operators (cont)"}

::::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
> **Do something, save result, overwriting original**

```{r}
#| label: overwrite
#| code-line-numbers: "5-6|7"
#| output-location: fragment

df <- tibble(
  x = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5), 
  y = c("a", "a", "b", "c", "c")
)
df <- df |>
  mutate(x = x * 2)
df
```
:::

::: {.column .fragment width="50%"}
> **Do something, save result, *not* overwriting original**

```{r}
#| label: no-overwrite
#| code-line-numbers: "5-6|7"
#| output-location: fragment

df <- tibble(
  x = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5), 
  y = c("a", "a", "b", "c", "c")
)
df_new <- df |>
  mutate(x = x * 2)
df
```
:::
:::::

## {.smaller .sparse-slide data-menu-title="Assignment operators (cont)"}

::::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
> **Do something, save result, overwriting original [when you
> shouldn't]{style="color: #E74C3C"}**

```{r}
#| code-line-numbers: "5-8"

df <- tibble(
  x = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5), 
  y = c("a", "a", "b", "c", "c")
)
df <- df |>
  group_by(y) |>
  summarize(mean_x = mean(x))
df
```
:::

::: {.column .fragment width="50%"}
> **Do something, save result, [not]{style="color: #18BC9C"} overwriting
> original [when you shouldn't]{style="color: #18BC9C"}**

```{r}
#| code-line-numbers: "5-8"

df <- tibble(
  x = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5), 
  y = c("a", "a", "b", "c", "c")
)
df_summary <- df |>
  group_by(y) |>
  summarize(mean_x = mean(x))
df
```
:::
:::::

## {.smaller .sparse-slide data-menu-title="Assignment operators (cont)"}

::::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
> **Do something, save result, overwriting original**\
> [***data frame***]{style="color: #18BC9C"}

```{r}
#| code-line-numbers: "5-6"

df <- tibble(
  x = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5), 
  y = c("a", "a", "b", "c", "c")
)
df <- df |>
  mutate(z = x + 2)
df
```
:::

::: {.column .fragment width="50%"}
> **Do something, save result, overwriting original**\
> [***column***]{style="color: #f39c12"}

```{r}
#| code-line-numbers: "5-6"

df <- tibble(
  x = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5), 
  y = c("a", "a", "b", "c", "c")
)
df <- df |>
  mutate(x = x + 2)
df
```
:::
:::::

## {.smaller .sparse-slide data-menu-title="Assignment operators (cont)"}

::::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
> **Do something and show me**

```{r}
#| label: mutateB
#| code-line-numbers: "1-4|5-10|11-15"
#| eval: false

gss_all |>  
  select(year, agekdbrn) |> 
  filter(year == 2022) |> 
  drop_na()  |>
  mutate(age_groups = case_when(
    agekdbrn < 18 ~ "<18",
    agekdbrn >= 18 & agekdbrn <= 29 ~ "18–29",
    agekdbrn >= 30 & agekdbrn <= 39 ~ "30–39",
    agekdbrn >= 40 ~ "40+",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_)) |>
  group_by(age_groups) |>  
  summarise(
    count = n(),
    proportion = round(count / sum(count), 3)
  )

```

:::

::: {.column .fragment width="50%"}
> **Do something, save result, not overwriting original.**

```{r}
#| label: mutateA
#| code-line-numbers: "1-9|11-20"
#| eval: false

# Do something
gss_all <-  gss_all |>  
  mutate(age_groups = case_when(
    agekdbrn < 18 ~ "<18",
    agekdbrn >= 18 & agekdbrn <= 29 ~ "18–29",
    agekdbrn >= 30 & agekdbrn <= 39 ~ "30–39",
    agekdbrn >= 40 ~ "40+",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_)
  ) 

# Now show me
gss_all |>
  select(year, age_groups) |> 
  filter(year == 2022) |> 
  drop_na()  |>
  group_by(age_groups) |>  
  summarise(
    count = n(),
    proportion = round(count / sum(count), 3)
  )

```
:::
:::::

## Overwriting & raw data {.sparse-slide}

[Never overwrite your raw dataset!]{style="color: #E74C3C; font-size: 175%; font-family: 'Shadows Into Light'"} 

<br>

::: {.callout-tip icon="false"}
## {{< fa hat-wizard >}} Heads Up!

Always save transformed data as a new object, which should remain untouched for reference and reproducibility.

:::

## `write_rds()` & `read_rds()` {.sparse-slide}

`write_rds()` saves an R object to a file  
`read_rds()` loads an R object from a .rds file

<br>

. . .

```{r}
#| label: save-load
#| eval: false
#| code-line-numbers: "1|3"

write_rds(my_data, "my_data_file.rds") # <1>

read_rds("my_data_file.rds") # <2>

```

1.  Saves your df in current working directory
2.  Opens your df if in current working directory

# Think Like a Statistician {background-image="images/lightbulb-solid.png" background-size="80px" background-repeat="repeat"}

In 2024, how did the average amount of television watched differ between married people and those who were never married? And how did it compare to people who were widowed, divorced, or separated?

<br>

[{{< fa regular lightbulb >}} **How do we find
out?**]{style="color: #F39C12; font-size: 175%; font-family: 'Shadows Into Light'"}


## {data-menu-title="Think Like a Statistician" background-image="images/lightbulb-solid.png" background-size="80px" background-repeat="repeat"}

Use `select()`, `filter()`, `mutate()`, `group_by()`, & `summarise()`

<br>

. . .

::: {style="color: #f39c12; font-size: 200%;  font-family: 'Shadows Into Light'"}
{{< fa regular lightbulb >}} **Can you reproduce this table?**
:::

```{r}
#| label: think-output
#| echo: false

gss_all |> 
  select(year, marital, tvhours) |>
  filter(year == 2024) |>
  drop_na() |>
  mutate(mar_cat = case_when(
    marital == 1 ~ "Married",
    marital > 1 & marital < 5 ~ "Widow/div/sep",
    marital == 5 ~ "Never married",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_)) |>
  group_by(mar_cat) |>  
  summarise(
    count = n(),
    mean = round(mean(tvhours), digits = 2), 
    median = round(median(tvhours)),
    sd = round(sd(tvhours), digits = 2)
    ) 
```

::: aside
`tvhours`: Hours per day watching tv  
`marital`: Are you currently – married, widowed, divorced, separated, or have you never been married?
:::
